summary: Tenant isolation as the product itself guards it: its tenant-SQL check, which fails on any new query over a tenant table that neither filters by organisation nor says how it is scoped, and its row-level security check (every tenant table under a policy for the tenant role, then a live two-organisation probe), run on an embedded throwaway database. (Its per-tool isolation sweep runs in the functional lane's smoke row, which it ends.) Then a row per pack (packs.tables): every table a pack creates under row-level security, forced, with a policy.
not_covered: check:rls here runs on an embedded throwaway database (PGlite) built by the product's own migrations: it proves the migrations put row-level security in place, not that the deployed database has it. The deployed database is proven by the deploy itself (provision.py runs the same check against it and records datastores.postgres.rls_verified; a failure is a failed health check).
Queries the product's baseline file lists as pending review (scripts/tenant-sql-baseline.json) are reported by the product's own check, not failed.

packs.tables reads the catalog per pack; the live two-workspace probe of the same tables is check:rls. A host pack's tables are still the shell's base schema (mold_v0-049), so its row says it has none of its own, not-covered rather than pass.
